title: Operator-escrowed gated enactor for Optimize recommendations
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Implement an operator-escrowed gated enactor that safely applies batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations produced by Optimize. This feature provides a predictable path from recommendation -> simulated validation -> limited canary -> operator escrow approval -> phased activation with automatic rollback windows.

Motivation: Fully automated application of cost-saving configuration has caused operational surprises in a handful of pilot customers. Teams want lower manual overhead but need strong guardrails: reproducible simulated verification, traffic partitioning (golden vs production), an explicit operator escrow step with a clear recovery window, and improved observability for root-cause and audit.

Scope:
- Backend: recommendation dispatcher, simulation harness, canary policy engine, escrow state machine, rollback orchestrator.
- Console: operator escrow UI, canary dashboard slice, approve/reject workflow, one-click rollback.
- Telemetry: SLO delta checks, token-level cost delta, per-route error and latency histograms, and an explainability blob for why a recommendation was chosen.
- Runbook: operator playbook for common failure modes, and an automated incident stub that captures recent model + infra deltas.

Non-goals: full autonomous autodeploy without any operator step; replacing existing RBAC model (we will integrate with current RBAC).
acceptance_criteria: Simulated validation: for any Optimize recommendation the simulation harness produces a pass/fail with metric deltas and token-level sample diffs.
Canary gating: canary policy can route 1% and 10% traffic windows and enforce SLO thresholds (latency, error rate, hallucination proxy) before escalation to operator escrow.
Operator escrow: operators can approve or reject from Console; approval writes an immutable audit record and triggers phased activation policy.
Rollback automation: if SLO degradation exceeds threshold during a rollout window, the system auto-rolls back to previous config and emits alert with remediation steps.
Observability: canary dashboard shows before/after per-model and per-route costs, token breakdown, latency p50/p95 and error spikes; logs are retained for 90 days.
E2E tests: integration test that exercises recommendation -> simulate -> canary -> approve -> phased rollout -> rollback triggers under injected fault.
tasks: Design and implement simulation harness (backend) to run recommendations against recent traffic snapshots
Implement canary policy engine supporting traffic partitions, ramp schedules and SLO checks
Build escrow state machine and persistent audit records (immutable, signed)
Console UI: operator escrow panel, canary timeline, approve/reject actions and rollback button
Telemetry: SLO calculators, cost delta estimators, sample diff collector and explainability payloads
Runbook and playbook: create ops runbook + Slack alerting templates and incident stub
Integration tests: add e2e with fault injection and simulated traffic
Security review: vet audit storage and KMS signing for escrow records
notes: This ticket unifies prior work on simulated canaries and rollout orchestration into a single operator-centric flow. The design emphasizes a short recovery window and explicit human-in-the-loop approval to reduce blast-radius while preserving automation benefits.
risks: False negative in simulation (simulation passes but production degrades) — mitigated by conservative SLO thresholds and short ramp windows
Operator fatigue from noisy recommendations — mitigated by priority scoring and batching of low-impact suggestions
Complex rollback interactions with concurrent config changes — mitigated by serializing enactor transactions per-customer and version pinning
